title: OS AI Game Engine to make games (currently free unlimited chat)
author: Soft_Negotiation3487
selftext: If you are tired of the back and forth from the ChatGPT/Claude tab and your game engine, finding it frustrating that it can't understand your context, this could help you get some speed into releasing that game you're working on the side :)  It is OS and based on OG Godot

comments.author: MrPhil
comments.body: Have you solved the log/errors issue?  I'd love to stop needing to screenshot and paste syntax errors.

replies.author: Soft_Negotiation3487
replies.body: thanks, is this for the debugger live? it should be working for the output, we can add the debugger as well. lmk if the issue is sth else

replies.author: MrPhil
replies.body: What I mean is I use Claude Code with Godot currently.  There are errors, and warnings that don't goto the log Claude can access.  So, if say the syntax error occurs, I have to screenshot the error in the editor and then paste it into Claude.  If you've exposed those in way Claude can read them.without me have to intervene then that would be worth a lot to me.

comments.author: dragonboltz
comments.body: I gave this a try the other day and it’s pretty cool for whipping up little demos without tabbing back and forth between ChatGPT and your engine. It’s definitely still rough around the edges but the concept of an AI game engine is super interesting. On the asset side I’ve been experimenting with Meshy as a quick way to get low poly models from text prompts – it’s great for placeholders when you’re just prototyping mechanics. Curious to see how this project evolves!

replies.author: Soft_Negotiation3487
replies.body: Hey we just made the repo publicly available when I posted it :) not sure how you gave it a try before - meshy is great, would love to chat over discord and see how we can help you for 3d/meshy assets

comments.author: TheMisterPirate
comments.body: Will you be keeping parity with new releases of Godot and whatever features they add? I am starting a project and just started learning Godot with the plan to use AI heavily. Was thinking to just use VS Code + Kilocode alongside Godot, but wondering what the advantages of this would be?
